Get started

Inbundly bundles together emails that share the same labels. Bundles make it easier to manage and view related emails.

To get the most out of Inbundly, you can set up bundles by creating Gmail filters. Read on to learn about setting up bundles, key features, and preferred Gmail settings.

Set up bundles by creating filters

Inbundly uses labels to bundle messages. You can set up Gmail filters to automatically label emails that match criteria that you specify. When you receive these emails, Inbundly will display them in a bundle corresponding to their label.

There are a few ways to create and manage filters. The search box offers an easy way to create a new filter.

1
Open the search form
Click the down arrow to open the form on the search bar.
2
Enter filter criteria
Fill out the form with criteria to match messages of interest, ex. enter “*@acme.com” in the “From” field to filter email from the acme.com domain.
3
Choose a label
Check “Apply the label” and select a label. Then click “Create filter” to save the filter.

Bundles & colors

A few options (under Options) control how bundles are grouped and colored:

  • Combine labels. Instead of one bundle per label, each distinct set of labels forms its own bundle — so threads labeled A + B are grouped separately from those labeled just A. The bundle title factors out any shared parent (e.g. IH/AI + Bender).
  • Priority bundles. Force chosen labels (or label sets) to always bundle together, whatever else a thread carries — e.g. Bank keeps every bank thread in one bundle, School/* also folds in its sub-labels, and Work + Urgent captures threads with both. Rules are checked top to bottom; the first match wins.
  • Single-item bundles. Labels with only one thread are shown as regular messages instead of a one-row bundle (on by default).
  • Bundle colors. Tint each bundle to match its Gmail label color, either by filling the row background with a subtle tint or by coloring just the left accent bar and text. Works in both light and dark themes.
  • Stylus theme-matching. If you theme Gmail with a Stylus userstyle, enable Catppuccin color-matching to snap bundle colors to the active flavor's palette so they look native to the theme.

Pinning messages

You can pin important bundled messages by starring them. By default, pinned messages appear in their own row outside of their bundle. You can turn this behavior off under Options → Bundle setup if you prefer starred messages to remain bundled.

The pinned-messages toggle is optional and hidden by default — turn it on under Options → Features.

Archiving messages

Messages in a bundle can be archived easily, with a single click. You can archive all messages in a bundle, that are on the current page. Messages in each date section can also be archived in the same way.

The archive-all button is optional and hidden by default — turn it on under Options → Features.

Preferred Gmail settings

Inbundly primarily supports the default Gmail settings. Here are the recommended settings that work best with Inbundly:

  • Default inbox type. Inbundly supports this layout regardless of whether the category tabs are shown (Primary, Social, Promotions, etc.).
  • Show 100 conversations per page (the maximum number).
  • English language. When Gmail is not using English, bundling may work, but the date sections will not appear.
  • Labels should be shown in the message list, which is the default behavior. Inbundly reads label colors from the message list, so bundle coloring needs this on.

Options

All options below (and custom bundles) sync to your other browsers signed into the same Chrome or Firefox account, via chrome.storage.sync.

Bundle setup

Labels Add the name of each bundle on a new line. For nested labels, use forward-slashes between the nesting hierarchy levels. Add a trailing “/*” to a label to also include its sub-labels — e.g. “Newsletters/*” matches Newsletters and everything nested under it. Matching is case-insensitive.

Date grouping

Group messages by date

Starred messages

Keep starred messages outside bundles (Inbox-style pinning)

Appearance

Bundle colors

Color bundles to match their Gmail label color

Features

Show the pinned-messages toggle in the search bar
Show the archive-all button on bundles and date sections

Advanced

Combine labels

Bundle each distinct set of labels together (e.g. threads labeled A + B form their own bundle)

Priority bundles One rule per line. A rule captures matching threads into a single bundle, overriding combined-label grouping. Join labels with “+” to require several at once, and add a trailing “/*” to also include a label's sub-labels. Rules are checked top to bottom; the first match wins.

Force specific labels (or label sets) to always bundle together, regardless of the other labels a thread carries. Add a trailing /* to also include a label's sub-labels, or join labels with + to capture threads that carry all of them. Rules are checked top to bottom; the first match wins.

Single-item bundles

Skip bundling labels that only have one thread — show them as regular messages

Stylus theme matching

If you theme Gmail with a Stylus userstyle, Inbundly can match bundle colors to the theme's palette instead of Gmail's default label colors.

Enable Catppuccin color-matching

Custom bundles
Custom bundles are ad-hoc groups you make by selecting messages in Gmail and clicking “Bundle selected” — no Gmail label required. They stick across reloads and sync to your other signed-in Chrome or Firefox browsers, like every other option on this page. Manage or clean them up here; changes apply immediately (no Save needed).

    No custom bundles yet. In Gmail, select some messages and click “Bundle selected” to make one.

    Sync & backup
    Settings travel through your browser account, but only between installs that share one extension ID. Unpacked builds derive their ID from the “key” in manifest.json — without it, each computer gets its own ID and its own private copy of these settings. Export/Import moves settings over by hand.

    This install's extension ID is … — sync only reaches installs with the same ID, so it should read the same on every computer (compare it at chrome://extensions).

    About Inbundly

    Inbundly is an open-source browser extension that brings bundles to Gmail. To learn more, visit inbundly.com.

    This build is a fork of the original teresa-ou/inboxy, with added options for combined-label bundles, bundle coloring, and Stylus theme-matching, so it differs from the published extension.
